title: Domain, invertibility and counit equation for exceptional coefficient mates
statement: The first two conjuncts of the exceptional coefficient comparison theorem: bounded constructible finite-Tor objects remain in the exceptional domain, and the canonical quotient comparison is invertible with its counit-transpose identity.

source.place: Domain check and counit-transpose calculation in the proof of compatibility (2).

proof.text: For the coefficient ring ULift (ULift (ZMod (l^r))), the positive integer l^r annihilates the ring and is invertible on Y: lift the given stalkwise unit l to global sections and take its r-th power. Choose a Tor interval [a,b] for K. Apply the source-library theorem constructibleTorAmplitudeIn_rightDerivedUpperShriek_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension, which uses the smooth tensor formula and the flat constructible rank-one dualizing line. It gives bounded constructibility and Tor interval [a-2d,b-2d], hence the required domain preservation.

At the exceptional image, apply the already proved compactSupportMap_isIso. On its compactification, the proper map has Noetherian source because it is proper over Y. The proper scalar mate is invertible on every input by properFiniteCoefficientExtension; the open comparison is an isomorphism by construction.

Unfold mateMap. Apply the inverse of the exceptional adjunction Hom equivalence to its defining transpose. The inverse/apply identity is exactly the displayed counit equation; invertibility of the exceptional coefficient mate is neither assumed nor needed.
